Bayesian VAR

Source: R/bvar.R
bvarm.Rd

Estimates a Bayesian VAR. The default conjugate Minnesota prior is sampled exactly for fixed hyperparameters and with a compiled Metropolis-within-direct-draws sampler for hierarchical hyperparameters (Giannone-Lenza-Primiceri 2015). Everything inside the MCMC loop is C++.

bvarm(
  Y,
  p = 4L,
  prior = prior_minnesota(),
  ndraw = 5000L,
  nburn = 2000L,
  const = TRUE,
  trend = FALSE,
  exog = NULL,
  scale = 0.5,
  adapt = TRUE,
  sv = FALSE,
  thin = 1L,
  sv_prior = c(a = 5, b = 0.04, V0 = 10),
  store_h = FALSE
)

Arguments

Y

numeric matrix, data frame or ts (T x K) of endogenous variables.

p

lag order.

prior

prior_minnesota() (conjugate, exact/hierarchical) or prior_triangular() (equation-by-equation sampler: Minnesota, SSVS or horseshoe, optional stochastic volatility).

ndraw

number of retained posterior draws.

nburn

burn-in iterations (hierarchical sampler only).

const

include a constant.

trend

include a linear trend.

exog

optional T x q matrix of exogenous regressors (contemporaneous, treated like deterministic terms; future values are then required for forecasting).

scale

initial scale of the random-walk proposal.

adapt

adapt the proposal scale during burn-in towards 25-45% acceptance.

sv

stochastic volatility (random-walk log-volatility, Kim-Shephard-Chib mixture) – only with prior_triangular().

thin

keep every thin-th draw (triangular sampler).

sv_prior

c(a, b, V0): inverse-gamma(a, b) prior on the log-volatility innovation variance (default mean 0.01) and prior variance V0 of the initial log-volatility.

store_h

store the full volatility draws (ndraw x T x K); the posterior mean path is always kept.

Value

a bvarm object. Use irf(), fevd(), hd(), forecast(), stability(); $draws is a draws object, $hyper the retained hyperparameter draws, $logml the log marginal likelihood at the mode (or fixed values).

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- bvarm(yraw, p = 4, ndraw = 2000, nburn = 1000)
fit
#> <bvarm> niw-minnesota BVAR(4), K = 3, 2000 posterior draws
#> log marginal likelihood: -407.87452
#> hyperparameters (posterior mean [5%, 95%]); MH acceptance 0.346
#>          mean     5%    95%
#> lambda 0.3610 0.2538 0.5137
#> soc    1.1115 0.5250 2.1449
#> sur    0.6302 0.1836 1.6041
#> 
#> posterior mean of B:
#>            X1      X2      X3
#> X1.l1  1.4120  0.0312  0.4000
#> X2.l1 -0.2222  1.2522 -0.5827
#> X3.l1 -0.0423 -0.0291  0.7946
#> X1.l2 -0.3273 -0.0044 -0.3214
#> X2.l2  0.1123 -0.2804  0.4873
#> X3.l2  0.0361  0.0050 -0.0107
#> X1.l3 -0.0890 -0.0469  0.2139
#> X2.l3  0.0295 -0.1092 -0.0257
#> X3.l3  0.0033  0.0545  0.0969
#> X1.l4  0.0021  0.0481 -0.1854
#> X2.l4  0.0383  0.0401  0.1333
#> X3.l4 -0.0012 -0.0070  0.0245
#> const  0.2778  0.3525  0.0506
plot(irf(fit, horizon = 16))
